jobs.title: Director of Product Management
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Retail media is CommerceIQ's biggest and fastest-growing product line, and it sits inside one of the fastest-growing categories in all of advertising. US retail media ad spend is growing roughly 18% year over year in 2026, nearly double the growth rate of digital advertising overall, and it's on track to keep outpacing search and social for years to come.

We have a real chance to be the world's best at this. Not the best software vendor, the best at actually delivering the outcome: incremental sales lift from media investment. We already have a significant lead here through our work on incrementality measurement, we can prove the sales lift our customers get from their media spend in a way most of the market can't. What we need now is someone who can take that lead and turn it into a category-defining, agentic product.

How We Go to Market

Our model is services as software: an agent plus a managed services team working together, owning the outcome for the customer rather than just handing them a dashboard. This role is about taking that model and re-architecting it, from a SaaS + services model to an agent-native services product line, one that can scale 10x over the next one to two years without scaling headcount at the same rate.

What You'll Own

Own delivery and execution for the entire retail media product line, and build and lead the team that drives it.

Partner closely with the VP, Retail Media to shape strategy and roadmap, then run the execution
requirements: 8-17 years of experience in product management or equivalent roles, with a track record owning delivery and execution for a meaningful, revenue-generating product line, ideally one you scaled significantly.
Genuinely AI-forward: you've built or shipped with LLMs, agents, and modern AI tooling, not just read about them.
Experience running a team while partnering closely with a peer or senior leader on strategy.
Strong instincts for customer-facing work: you can sit with a customer, understand their workflow, and translate it into product.
Experience partnering closely with engineering and with sales/GTM teams.
High ownership and comfort operating as the de facto GM of this product line's delivery.
Bachelor's degree, preferably in Business, Computer Science, or a related field.
preferred: Retail media or ad tech experience.
Background in incrementality measurement, marketing mix modeling, or media attribution.
Prior experience taking a SaaS product agentic.

Its suite of products — including the Greenlight app, debit card, Safe Family GPS trackers, and Family Hub — brings together financial tools, safety features, and everyday family management in one connected experience. jobs.title: Director of Product
jobs.description:
Director of Product

AI Cloud and Orchestration, Velocis Platform

Reports to Chief Product Officer

Location Mumbai

Function Product Leadership, AI Infrastructure (Velocis)

Why this role, why now?

Neysa is building the AI cloud for the era where AI runs in production rather than in pilots. The promise we are claiming to deliver is operational confidence, the ability for an enterprise to run AI predictably, affordably and accountably. Infrastructure choices now decide which AI programmes are viable at all, and for us sovereignty means strategic control rather than a compliance checkbox.

Velocis is how we deliver that, across GPU as a service and our AI platform as a service. We are scaling from strong early proof into a platform that serves sovereign enterprise buyers in India and large offtake capacity globally. This role exists to help set product direction and to make it real.
responsibilities: We are hiring a Senior Director of Product to sit alongside the Chief Product Officer as a balanced strategist and operator, and to co-own the Velocis product ecosystem. You will help shape the two-year product strategy and you will own the roadmap, prioritisation and specification sign-off that turn it into shipped platform. Engineering, infrastructure operations, design and go-to-market are your delivery partners, and product holds the pen on what gets built and in what order.
You will move between whiteboarding high-density cluster architecture with an executive buyer in one hour and running a deep specification review with a product manager in the next. Both are the job.
What you will own?Product strategy and roadmap
Co-own the 12 and 24 month strategy for Velocis across GPU as a service and the AI platform, and hold the roadmap, prioritisation and specification sign-off end to end.
Ship the Velocis AI platform stack and move straight into post-launch feature velocity, reliability, and the Day-0 and Day-1 user journey.
Keep a live read on the global AI infrastructure landscape, across orchestration layers, sovereign cloud, inference economics and power and density, so Velocis holds its edge.
Team and craft
Lead, mentor and hold accountable a team of four or more product managers across the core Velocis modules.
Build a product culture of extreme ownership, technical precision and fast feedback, and raise the hiring bar as the team grows.
Coach high-potential talent and step in where a track needs lift.
Enterprise commercials and offtake
Partner with the CPO and CEO on offtake opportunities from 1,000 to 8,000 GPUs, shaping orchestration specs, tenant isolation and SLA commitments.
requirements: Ten or more years in product management, with four or more leading product teams. Hands-on experience in GPU computing, AI or ML orchestration or HPC is ideal, and strong candidates from adjacent large-scale cloud or general-purpose cloud infrastructure, with the ability to ramp fast, will be considered.
A track record of shipping complex B2B infrastructure products from concept to meaningful revenue scale.

Fluency across GPU infrastructure on NVIDIA and AMD, container and workload orchestration such as Kubernetes, Slurm and Ray, VPC and network topologies, object storage and dedicated inference pipelines.

Working command of multi-tenancy and tenant isolation, observability and cost attribution, sovereign deployment patterns such as air-gapped clusters and customer-managed keys, and inference economics measured as cost per token and P99 latency.
Commercial fluency, so that you connect product decisions to gross margin, resource efficiency and customer return.
How you work?
You zoom out to market positioning and a two-year horizon, and zoom in to specifications, telemetry and the granular detail, without losing either.
You have a default to action and high standards, and you pair them with the judgment to say no and to sequence well.
You are a low-ego and articulate communicator who earns credibility quickly with engineers, enterprise CTOs and executive leadership.
You are comfortable building in a category that is still being created.
Your first 90 days
Take full ownership of the roadmap and prioritisation across the PM tracks, with clear ownership lines in place.

responsibilities: Where does automation earn trust, and where does a human still need to stay in the loop?

You will work hand-in-hand with Engineering, Design, Content, Data, and Marketing to ship a product that moves real numbers and real lives.

Own the full growth loop: Activation Engagement Habit Formation Retention for DBMCI One learners across platforms.
Define and drive the product roadmap for learner-facing features, from discovery through experimentation, launch, and post-launch iteration.

jobs.title: Product Owner
jobs.description:
Job Description

This is a remote position.

Experience Level

We're looking for a seasoned Product Owner with at least 2–4 years of experience owning a product backlog end-to-end within an Agile delivery environment. You should be a "delivery craftsperson" who can demonstrate a track record of turning ambiguous, cross-team requirements into shipped, working software — with particular comfort operating inside platforms where your product's success depends on coordination with teams you don't manage.
responsibilities: As a Product Owner, you will own the backlog and delivery cadence for one product within a tightly interconnected platform, where your product's roadmap depends on — and feeds into — several sibling products. You'll act as the point of alignment between engineering teams, supporting product managers, and client stakeholders, translating business and compliance needs into backlog items ready for a development team to execute against.

A key part of the role is holding the line on requirements quality: defining clear acceptance criteria before work enters a sprint, and sequencing competing demands — new features, maintenance of live services, and production support — that your team carries simultaneously. Because your product does not operate in isolation, a large part of the job is coordinating dependencies across teams that don't report to you.
Backlog Ownership & Requirements Definition: Own and prioritize the product backlog; define acceptance criteria for accuracy, completeness, and readiness before stories are marked sprint-ready.

Cross-Team Dependency Coordination: Sequence and negotiate delivery across multiple dependent engineering teams (platform, integration, infrastructure, and adjacent product teams), since most features require multi-team scheduling rather than single-team execution.

Delivery Prioritization Under Competing Demands: Balance new feature development, maintenance of live production services, and active production support within the same backlog, without letting one silently starve the others.

Domain Ramp-Up: Build working depth in the specific technical and regulatory domain tied to your assigned product — this may include healthcare EDI transaction standards, web-automation/data-extraction reliability, credential and access-security models, or regulated payments and remittance processing, depending on placement.

Stakeholder & Requirements Governance: Partner with the supporting Product Manager and client-side stakeholders to close open requirement decisions before development starts, hold sign-off discipline, and manage rework risk from late-stage scope changes.

Data & Interface Quality Ownership: Where your product's output feeds downstream systems, own the interface contract (field definitions, data completeness, naming) to prevent avoidable rework further down the chain.
requirements: Proven Product Ownership Experience: Track record owning a backlog end-to-end in an Agile environment, ideally within a platform where products are tightly coupled rather than independent.

Domain Adaptability: Comfort ramping quickly into unfamiliar technical or regulatory domains — some assignments require near-immediate fluency (e.g., regulated payments, EDI standards), while others allow for a longer runway.
Cross-Functional Coordination Skills: Demonstrated ability to sequence work and resolve competing priorities across multiple engineering teams that don't report into the same chain.
Analytical Rigor: Ability to write precise, testable acceptance criteria and reason through data quality or completeness gaps before they become delivery blockers.
Strong Stakeholder Communication: Comfortable representing product status and trade-offs to both engineering teams and client-facing stakeholders, in plain, non-technical language when needed.

Judgment Under Ambiguity: Able to recognize when a decision needs escalation versus independent ownership — particularly important for the more regulation-heavy assignments, where working without senior support isn't advisable early on.

This is a builder's role. Define and own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for an agentic AI product built from zero — problem discovery, architecture direction, MVP scoping, and scale-up.

Run structured discovery with enterprise customers and internal stakeholders to identify high-value workflows for autonomous or semi-autonomous automation.

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager
responsibilities: Agentic Investigation & Reliability Experiences
Sumo Logic is hiring a Principal Product Manager to lead how engineers and operators investigate incidents, understand reliability risk, and act on their operational and security telemetry.

The observability category was built around collecting telemetry and giving people tools to navigate it: dashboards, queries, monitors, traces, and alerts. Customer expectations are now shifting. Teams don't just want more dashboards; they want help getting from a signal to a resolution, understanding what's broken, why, what's impacted, and what to do next. As AI agents move into production operations, this role owns how Sumo Logic brings intelligent, agent-assisted investigation and reliability workflows to customers, grounded in evidence, context, and enterprise governance.

This is a senior, high-ownership role. It requires genuine observability domain background. You should have lived in this space and understand how monitoring, troubleshooting, and reliability actually work, combined with the ambition to define a new category of experience on top of it.
What You Will Own
The current data experiences.

Log Search, Live Tail, query and query optimization, Metrics Search, Tracing, Dashboards, and the data-experience UI. This is a live, revenue-generating product with real customers, and keeping it strong is part of the job. You own its health, roadmap, and competitiveness today while steering it toward an AI-native future, focusing new investment where it strengthens investigation, speed, and value for both new and power users.
The reliability and alerting surface.

Monitors, Alerts, SLOs, Scheduled Searches, and the reliability workflows around them. You will own alerting accuracy, noise reduction, and operational health signals both as capabilities customers depend on today and as the foundation for more automated, agent-assisted detection and investigation.
The agentic investigation experience.

You will define how a user moves from a search, a monitor, a dashboard, or an alert to likely cause faster, with supporting evidence. This means productizing investigation workflows that reason across logs, metrics, traces, monitors, dashboards, and related context, and evolving them from reactive troubleshooting toward more proactive detection over time.
What You Will Be Doing
requirements: 8+ years of product management experience with real observability or monitoring domain background. You have owned products in observability, monitoring, incident response, APM, or a closely adjacent operational-telemetry space. This is a hard requirement.

Deep, first-hand understanding of the observability surface area including logs, metrics, traces, dashboards, monitors, alerts, and SLOs, and of how engineers and operators actually investigate incidents and decide what to trust.
Proven ability to run a live, at-scale product, owning the roadmap, health, and competitiveness of shipping surfaces while driving a larger transformation.
A track record of owning broad, technically deep surfaces and setting direction that other teams build on.
Familiarity with how AI and agents are changing data interaction, including natural-language investigation, tools, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop action, or the ability to ramp quickly.

Strong technical instincts around query engines, time-series and trace data, and alerting systems, plus the judgment to know where an AI-assisted experience should replace a manual flow and where depth must stay.
Strong analytical skills and comfort using telemetry, dashboards, SQL, and usage data to understand adoption, friction, reliability, and cost.
Excellent communication across technical and business audiences, and the ability to write clear proposals, decision docs, PRDs, and acceptance criteria.
High ownership and drive to make progress across a large, ambiguous, fast-moving surface.
Must-Have Qualities
Runs today, builds tomorrow.
Keeps a live product healthy and competitive while reinventing it, and knows what to sustain and what to rebuild.

Async-first. Documentation and written communication are how decisions travel across time zones

Changing the world through digital experiences is what Adobe’s all about. We give everyone—from emerging artists to global brands—everything they need to design and deliver exceptional digital experiences. We’re on a mission to hire the very best and are committed to building exceptional employee experiences where everyone is respected and has access to equal opportunity. We realize that new ideas can come from everywhere in the organization, and we know the next big idea could be yours!

Adobe Express is building the next generation of AI-powered creative experiences used by hundreds of millions of creators worldwide. We're looking for a Product Manager who is passionate about building intelligent creative experiences and bringing ground breaking AI capabilities to customers worldwide. Partner closely with Engineering, Design, Applied Research, Adobe Firefly, and Imaging Platform teams to bring ground breaking AI capabilities into intuitive creative workflows.
Collaborate with Growth teams to improve activation, engagement, retention, and monetization across the customer journey.
Coordinate complex launches across multiple cross-functional teams while balancing customer value, technical feasibility, and business impact.
Continuously simplify creative workflows and find chances to define AI-powered editing faster, more intuitive, and more delightful.
What You'll Work On
Depending on business priorities, you'll contribute to initiatives such as:
AI-powered photo enhancement

2-6 years of Product Management experience building and shipping consumer or SaaS products.
Strong product intuition with a deep customer-first perspective.
Experience partnering closely with Engineering, Design, Data Science, and cross-functional collaborators.
Strong analytical abilities with experience defining critical metrics, interpreting product analytics, and running experiments.
Experience building AI-powered customer experiences.
Excellent communication, collaboration, and collaborator management skills.
Demonstrated experience owning products from concept through launch with measurable customer or business impact.
preferred: Familiarity with Generative AI, Computer Vision, LLMs, multimodal AI, or intelligent creative technologies.
Experience partnering with Applied Research or Machine Learning teams to translate AI capabilities into customer-facing products.

Experience building products used by millions of customers.

Adobe is redefining digital creativity through AI-powered experiences that empower creators of every skill level. Join a team solving challenging product problems at global scale while working alongside world-class engineers, designers, researchers, and AI experts to invent the future of creativity.

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.description:
Technology is one of the most important parts of our business. Whether it’s supporting our songwriters, ensuring we provide the right royalty data to global partners, or helping our creative teams use the latest AI tools to discover new talent, technology plays an invaluable role in our success. Product Managers help turn vision into reality.

We are looking for a Product Manager to partner with a local in-person engineering team in Bengaluru focused on music distribution. Distribution is the vital link between music creation and a fan’s headphones, ensuring our music reaches platforms like Spotify and YouTube globally while protecting the complex rights that ensure our artists get paid. You will be a "user-first" thinker who is responsible for a portfolio of features and products, navigating the high-stakes world of global rights, supply chain automation, and high-scale digital delivery.
responsibilities: Continuous Discovery:

Build deep empathy for our labels, operations teams, and global partners by maintaining a constant dialogue with them. Uncover their underlying pain points, ensuring that every solution we build truly solves their problems and makes their daily workflows more seamless.
Strategy & Roadmap:
Define and communicate the long-term vision and roadmap for your products, ensuring they align with WMG’s broader tech strategy.
Product Trio Collaboration:
Work in a "Product Trio" alongside Engineering and Design to solve complex problems, resolving trade-offs and tackling risks.
Execution & Ownership:
Serve as the primary author of PRDs and the "executor-in-chief" for your projects, driving development from ideation through technical delivery.
Launch & Impact:

Develop comprehensive go-to-market strategies, including product positioning, internal messaging, and launch plans. You don't just "ship" code; you ensure the organization is ready to adopt it to achieve maximum impact.
Analytical Optimization:

Continuously monitor product performance metrics, user feedback, and market trends. Use this data to make informed prioritization decisions, identify areas for improvement, and manage technical debt to optimize the product over its entire lifecycle.
requirements: Experienced:
You have at least 5 years of product management experience, ideally with exposure to the music business or other digital media.
Technical & Business Savvy:
You can discuss system architecture with engineers and business constraints with executives, mitigating Value, Usability, Feasibility, and Business Viability risks upfront.
A Master Storyteller:
You own the "Why" and can easily adjust your communication style for different audiences, from developers to more senior stakeholders.
Biased to Action:
You have a proven ability to unstick a team, make difficult prioritization decisions, and navigate the ambiguity of a global business.
Humble Leader:
You have strong opinions, held weakly; you are quick to share credit with your team and accept responsibility when things don’t go as planned.
Mission-Driven:
You are a music fan motivated by the fact that your work directly impacts an artist’s ability to grow their career and get paid.

Define use cases with clear value hypotheses, success measures, and risk considerations.

requirements: 15+ years of experience as a Senior Product Manager / Principal PM / Product Leader with experience owning business outcomes or product portfolio performance

jobs.title: Product Manager
responsibilities: Hevo
The Hard Thing About Data

Most companies that claim to have a "data platform" have a dashboard with some charts and a dream. Hevo has something different. Something that took eight years to build and can't be bought. Over 2,000 companies send us their most sensitive data every single day. 100 billion events a month. Raw. Unfiltered. Before transformation, before aggregation, at the exact moment truth is created. That's not a product feature. That's trust, earned one customer at a time, over eight years, by not screwing up.

That position is now the foundation for something much bigger. We're building an Intelligence Layer on top of it, a system that reads across every data source a company runs, connects the signals that matter, and tells people what to do before they have to go looking for answers. We call it the Context Graph. It's real enough to show results. Early enough that the person who joins now defines what it becomes.
This is the moment. Not the moment after it's obvious. Now.
What You're Walking Into

You'll own a product pod. SaaS integrations, database connectors, or the Intelligence Layer, depending on where the biggest need is when you join. You own the backlog. More importantly, you own the why behind everything that gets built. You report directly to the CEO. In the first 3-6 months, your job is to make the foundation bulletproof, find the gaps in the platform, close them, and make the product sharper than it's ever been. After that, you move into the Intelligence Layer and help define what Hevo becomes in its next chapter.
What This Job Actually Is

Let's be honest about what great PMs do, and what mediocre ones do instead. Mediocre PMs write specs and hand them off. They synthesize feedback from CSMs and call it customer insight. They sit in architecture meetings and nod. They measure their own output in documents shipped, not outcomes delivered. That's not this job. This job is three things, done well, simultneously.

First: technical ownership. You will be in the room when architecture decisions get made. Not watching. Contributing. Pushing back. Asking the questions that change the direction of the decision. You need to understand how data pipelines work at a systems level, CDC, connectors, streaming, schema management, failure modes. If you can't hold your own in that room, engineering will stop inviting you to it. And they'll be right to.

Second: direct customer engagement. You talk to customers yourself. No intermediary. No secondhand summary. You hear the problem in the customer's own words, you sit with the complexity of it, and you own the translation into product decisions. If you're relying on a CSM to tell you what customers need, you will always be one step behind.

Third: making complexity simple. Hevo's product is deeply technical. The people who sell it and support it are not always. A big part of your job is taking complex system behavior and making it crisp and understandable, for Support, for CS, for Solutions Engineering, so they can represent the product confidently to customers. If internal teams are confused, customers will be too.
